conservation.help_by: Give wildlife space; pick reef-safe sunscreen and careful finning.
conservation.caution_against: Don’t feed fish, chase animals, or pocket living souvenirs.

life_info.eating: Shrimp and microbes that dye feathers pink-orange. Upside-down bill filters tiny food from water.
life_info.mating: Colony nesters with dramatic group dances.
life_info.habitat: Salty lagoons and shallow flats with muddy bottoms. Huge pink flocks are a Caribbean postcard come alive.

fun_facts: You are what you eat — without pink prey, feathers fade.

life_info.eating: Crabs and snails drilled or pulled apart. Arms explore cracks while the body stays tucked.
life_info.mating: Female guards eggs; male uses a specialized arm.
life_info.habitat: Reef crevices and rubble; masters of hide-and-seek. Solitary geniuses with soft-body escape art.

fun_facts: Color and texture change in a blink — living camouflage.
Three hearts and blue blood keep the alien vibes strong.

conservation.help_by: Respect distance on the reef; support healthy fish stocks sharks need.
conservation.caution_against: Don’t bait, chase, or grab rays and sharks for photos.

life_info.eating: Reef fish and rays. Curious inspector that may circle divers — give space.
life_info.habitat: Drop-offs and reef walls with clear water and current. Often alone or in loose groups along a wall.

fun_facts: A classic reef-shark silhouette for Caribbean wall dives.
Healthy shark numbers usually mean a healthy reef pantry.

life_info.eating: Snails, crabs, and carrion. Antennae-first explorer of the night reef.
life_info.mating: Females carry eggs under the tail like an orange berry cluster.
life_info.habitat: Under coral ledges by day; marches across sand at night. Famous for single-file migration queues across the seafloor.

fun_facts: No big claws — defense is spines and a fast tail flip.
Long antennae combine touch and smell.
